🖥 Islamabad will always support Tehran, says Pakistan’s Parliament speaker

📌 Islamabad, IRNA – Pakistan’s National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq has called relations with Iran strong and unparalleled, urged deeper economic cooperation, and said Pakistan will always support Iran.

Ayaz Sadiq met with Fada-Hossein Maleki, Head of the Iran-Pakistan Parliamentary Friendship Group, on the sidelines of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Islamabad.
​
He emphasized parliamentary and economic cooperation between the two countries and the joint fight against terrorism, saying that Pakistan’s parliament was the first parliament in the world to condemn the US and Israeli attack on Iran and unanimously passed a resolution in this regard.
​
Ayaz Sadiq described the promotion of communications and the role of parliamentary friendship groups as important for strengthening relations, and called Gwadar Port an opportunity to expand trade between Iran and the countries of the region.
​
Emphasizing Pakistan’s continued support for Iran and Palestine, he described relations between the two countries as strong and unparalleled and stressed the need to increase bilateral trade and expand economic cooperation.
​
For his part, Maleki said that the Islamic Republic of Iran will never forget Pakistan’s support during difficult times, expressing gratitude for the efforts of Pakistan’s Prime Minister and Army Chief in mediating and de-escalating tensions in the region.

🌍 Araghchi meets Pakistan’s Army chief to discuss regional security

📌 Islamabad, IRNA - Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met with Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, Chief of Army Staff of Pakistan, as part of his bilateral meetings on the sidelines of the ECO Council of Foreign Ministers summit held in Islamabad.

During the meeting at the Army Command Headquarters in Rawalpindi on Monday evening, Araghchi and Munir reviewed the latest developments in bilateral relations between Tehran and Islamabad and discussed regional developments.
​
Earlier, Araghchi held a separate bilateral meeting with his Pakistani counterpart, Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar.
​
Iran’s top diplomat also met with Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, alongside other ministers and senior officials participating in the summit.
​
During the meeting, the Pakistani prime minister welcomed the ECO member states’ foreign ministers and stressed the importance of strengthening regional cooperation and leveraging capacities to develop economic, trade, and transit relations among neighboring and regional countries.
